s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive skin lesions with upper respiratory tract involvement and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
Palatal perforation and stridor necessitating tracheostomy
Saddle nose deformity and destruction of ear cartilage
key_facts: Woman in her 30s
Lesions started as an erythematous papule on the face and progressed to larger plaques within 10 years
Involvement of the upper respiratory tract
History of wheezing and breathlessness
No history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
Multiple well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring
Cervical lymphadenopathy with multiple, nontender, discrete nodes
Anemia with hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Normal kidney function test, liver function test, fasting blood glucose, and urinalysis
Negative serologic analysis for HIV-1/2, antinuclear antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
Normal chest radiography
Punch skin biopsy showing infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts
Histopathology showing pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes

shortlist.label: Chromoblastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of chronic progressive skin lesions with central scarring and histopathology showing pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, along with the presence of pigmented yeasts, is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Leprosy
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's skin lesions, upper respiratory tract involvement, and cervical lymphadenopathy are consistent with leprosy, although the absence of nerve involvement and negative serologic tests make this diagnosis less likely

shortlist.label: Rhinoscleroma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's upper respiratory tract involvement, including palatal perforation and stridor, and the presence of chronic progressive skin lesions, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Mycetoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's chronic progressive skin lesions with central scarring and the presence of cervical lymphadenopathy are consistent with this diagnosis, although the lack of a clear history of trauma or exposure to a specific organism makes this diagnosis less likely

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's chronic progressive skin lesions, upper respiratory tract involvement, and cervical lymphadenopathy, along with the presence of anemia and systemic symptoms, are consistent with this diagnosis, although the lack of a clear history of lymphoma or other malignancy makes this diagnosis less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes in the histopathology, along with the growth of black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species in the fungal skin culture, are characteristic features of Chromoblastomycosis

rejected.label: Leprosy
rejected.why: Leprosy typically presents with sensory loss and peripheral nerve involvement, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Rhinoscleroma
rejected.why: Rhinoscleroma is a chronic granulomatous infection of the nose, but it does not typically present with skin plaques or lymphadenopathy as seen in this case

rejected.label: Mycetoma
rejected.why: Mycetoma typically presents with a triad of painless swelling, multiple sinuses, and discharge, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder that typically presents with pulmonary symptoms and does not typically present with skin plaques or lymphadenopathy as seen in this case
